The path and bash guard cores are the only decision point for the write/shell boundary of the sdd MCP server, of the Copilot hooks fallback and of the Claude Code hooks; no mechanism re-implements their rules (the Serena-command confinement of C002-IF-008 §1.1 and the `--cwd` confinement of §1.2 included), and the OpenCode permission rules are generated from the same allowlist with no `allow` rule wider than the forms the generated agents send need; a guard rule that a glob cannot follow is a replay difference (C002-IF-001 §6.3)
The sdd MCP server runs commands without a shell: it executes the words the bash guard core tokenised, applies the pipe-only entries in-process and does not run `.cmd` or `.bat` files

Every fault in the sdd MCP server or in a Copilot guard hook ends in a refusal: an error result that changed nothing, or a deny decision on standard output with exit code 2, which holds also where the host reports another non-zero code and fails closed (Copilot CLI, `docs/spikes/S-08-copilot-vscode.md §2.2`); no error path allows a call, and no deny relies on exit 0. These are not faults and are allowed: a readable Copilot hook input without `agent_type` (C002-REQ-320, C002-REQ-330; on VS Code 1.145.2, which sends no `agent_type` on PreToolUse, every readable input, so there a hook denies only on its own faults and the Architect agents' boundary is their tool lists and the sdd MCP server; defect D-052), an Architect agent's call under sdd MCP server enforcement (C002-REQ-330), a non-Architect subagent's call outside a repository with `.sdd/` or to a `read_only` tool (C002-REQ-329). Whatever the Copilot hook cannot place in these cases or in a class is denied (C002-REQ-328); the install command writes the guard hook before the agents it guards (C002-IF-007 §Install step 5)
Generation is deterministic: sorted traversal, LF line endings, UTF-8 without BOM, stable JSON key order, and no time stamp or machine path in any generated file
Mapping tables and wiring variants live in `plugins/architect/targets/`; no Claude Code agent preloads them, and the Claude Code staging of `npm run package` leaves the folder out
`architect-sdd` has no runtime dependency and no install script; its two entries bundle every package they import except Node.js built-ins

C001-CON-02 stays in force for the plugin

The runner tests with a stub host end every session of the OpenCode and Copilot CLI eval runners at 30 turns (C002-TS-614), at the session timeout of 20 minutes with `end_reason` `error` and no `cap` record (C002-TS-690), and at the spend cap of 0.50 USD by the spend-cap rule of C002-IF-010 §2.2. The runner tests of the Claude Code eval runner, under both auth modes (`--auth subscription`, on the notional cost, and `--auth api-key`), pass an Agent SDK stub `maxTurns` 30 and neither `maxBudgetUsd` nor `taskBudget`, with no budget in the prompt or the system prompt, and record the stub's end at `maxTurns` as `error_max_turns`; they read the notional cost by the queue rule of C002-IF-010 §2.2 Claude Code spend cap (no usage request for a message ID already seen, at most one request open, the IDs that arrive while one is open coalesced into exactly one follow-up), and stop the session themselves at the first reading of 0.50 USD or above by an interrupt and the close of the query, with one `cap` and one `cap-close` record, every later tool request denied with the usual message, and `metrics.result_subtype` `error_max_budget_usd` with the cost read after the interrupt, never cut to the cap; a session that ends by itself keeps its result's subtype and cost, also at or above the cap; a failed reading while the query is open (a refused usage request, no answer within 30 s, or an answer without a finite cost of at least 0) stops the session after the 5 s settle time, rejects `runSession` with `claude-code spend check failed: …`, books the cost read in a spend ledger entry and writes no result record, while a refusal at the session's own end or at the runner's close is ignored; and the OpenCode and Copilot CLI runners give their hosts no spend cap or turn cap, other than Copilot CLI's `--max-ai-credits` (C002-TS-614, C002-TS-702, C002-TS-703, C002-TS-704, C002-TS-705; defect D-031).
